original.target_description: Sentence-completion experiment: final binary logistic regression predicting to- versus ing-completion; V_TARGET_DIST: to main effect, controlling other retained predictors and its interaction with V_FREQ. German L1 advanced learners of English.

n.sample_role: Analytic sentence-completion observations, from 92 participants; not a participant n.
n.exclusions: Other-completions discarded from 560 completions by 94 subjects; retained 193 ing-responses and 176 to-responses by 92 subjects.
n.location: Printed pp. 175–176, section 3.2 and final-model classification denominator (PDF pp. 14–15 including cover).
n.quote: we discarded the ‘other’-completions, which left us with 193 ing-responses and 176 to-responses (by altogether 92 subjects). ... the exact classification accuracy achieved by the model is 277/369≈75.1%

es.location: Printed p. 176, Table 2, V_TARGET_DIST: to row (PDF p. 15 including cover; article p. 14).

p.location: Printed p. 176, Table 2, V_TARGET_DIST: to row.

replication.target_description: CEDEL2 cross-sectional relation between L1 Spanish and L2 Spanish token frequencies for preterit verbs, section 4.2.4. Located page-20 correlation measures token frequency, not the supplied description’s contingent frequency/distinctiveness predictor.

n.sample_role: Verbs (preterit) in the L1–L2 token-frequency regression/correlation; not participants or verb-token observations.
n.exclusions: Exact verb inclusion/exclusion criteria for this regression are not stated in the results paragraph. Corpus selection restricted essays to descriptive/narrative tasks, 50–500 words, and L2 writers to L1 English, ages 17–26, proficiency A1–B2 (pp. 167–168).
n.quote: results show an R2 value of 0.78 (r = 0.88, p < 2.2e-16) for the relation between L1 and L2 frequency regarding the 300 verbs in the preterit.

es.test_statistic: t = 32.36 (reported main effect of L1 frequency)
es.quote: results show an R2 value of 0.78 (r = 0.88, p < 2.2e-16) for the relation between L1 and L2 frequency regarding the 300 verbs in the preterit.

p.quote: results show an R2 value of 0.78 (r = 0.88, p < 2.2e-16) for the relation between L1 and L2 frequency regarding the 300 verbs in the preterit.

reported_success.location: Printed p. 181 / PDF p. 26, section 6, Summary and conclusions.
reported_success.quote: This finding proves that Wulff et al.’s (2009) conclusion for L2 English oral production generalizes to L2 Spanish writing.

notes: Original table prints odds ratio with superscript exponent 11; plain-text extraction flattens the exponent to 1011. The two assigned IDs identify the same original V_TARGET_DIST effect. Replication page 20 reports token-frequency correlations, not a test of distinctiveness; this is a known target mismatch, retained explicitly rather than merged with the DCA results on pp. 176–177. The narrative success verdict concerns generalization of Wulff et al. (2009), which is a different cited primary work from the assigned Gries and Wulff (2009) original; it is not an explicit claim of replicating that assigned original test.
